claims.text: TypeSafe AI opened early access to Jev, their SystemOne model, in the week before this post (September 2026).
GeoDeploy compares AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud regions offering managed Kubernetes, picks the best region per geo, and provisions Kubernetes via the Pulumi Automation API.
TypeSafe's Jev provides AI primitives (confidence scoring, multiple choice, yes/no noul questions) that let apps, agents and workflows make decisions based on context.
GeoDeploy fetches current prices from the AWS Price List API, the Azure Retail Prices API, and the Google Cloud Billing Catalog.
GeoDeploy's module registry supports EKS, AKS, GKE; ECR, ACR, Artifact Registry; and DNS through Route 53, NS1, or Cloudflare.
The Pulumi Automation API runs a preview and then an update, one stack per region, and GeoDeploy won't run unless cloud credentials pass readiness checks.
Every GeoDeploy run writes plan.json and plan.md files.

Jev provides three primitives: choice() returns the pick, a probability distribution across all options, and a confidence; score() rates against a rubric (GeoDeploy uses 10 levels); noul() answers a yes/no question with a single probability.
Because Jev only selects from closed sets, a hallucinated region or made-up Pulumi argument cannot happen by construction.
GeoDeploy sends Jev a shortlist of up to 40 priced candidates per geo in a single call.
The @typesafe-ai/sdk package exports choice, noul, and score, and TypeSafeClient has a systemOne method returning answers.
TypeSafe advises to "describe situations, not degrees" when writing rubrics.
GeoDeploy's ranking uses weight profiles: latency-optimized (default), balanced, residency-first, failure-domain, with specified weights.
GeoDeploy confidence thresholds: data residency 0.95; new cluster region 0.90; existing-stack region 0.75; ingress/autoscaling module 0.85; node-pool sizing 0.60; global floor 0.50.
On gate failure, API timeout/error, or unreachable upstream, GeoDeploy falls back to deterministic price comparison enforcing residency and constraints; `geodeploy explain` shows why each region won.

In self-driving mode (`geodeploy monitor`), resizes apply automatically above 0.85 confidence, are suggested for human approval between 0.70 and 0.85, and below 0.70 fall back to a deterministic per-region rule.
CPU utilization alone makes a poor autoscaling metric and is usually paired with other signals.
The Pulumi Automation API page exists at /automation/.
Having more choices usually meant more complexity and technical debt; agents can now handle provisioning and scaling decisions.
